topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic, context, and expectations regarding complement.

topics.label: Fundamentals of the complement cascade
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational architecture, naming conventions, and central role of component C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three distinct recognition pathways that converge to trigger complement activation on pathogen surfaces.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream effector mechanisms used by the complement system to destroy pathogens and promote inflammation.

topics.label: Regulation and host cell protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how host cells utilize regulatory proteins to prevent unintended complement activation and self-damage.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the clinical manifestations and disease risks resulting from deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the evolutionary strategies used by pathogens to evade complement-mediated killing, illustrated by Staphylococcus aureus.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic marks the conclusion of the lecture and previews the next topic in the course.
